known_facts_book1: The fairy girl Ruler of the Land of Oz, who watches the whole journey in her Magic Picture with Dorothy.
Studies Woot's case in her Magic Room before setting out, and travels in the Red Wagon behind the Sawhorse to meet the party at Jinjur's ranch.
Breaks the Scarecrow's and the Tin Woodman's enchantments easily with a small silver Wand, reasoning that yookoohoo magic could only make a straw bear of a straw man and a tin owl of a tin man.
Breaks Polychrome's enchantment only after a chain of experiments: Canary to Dove, Dove to Speckled Hen, Hen to rabbit, rabbit to Fawn, then powders on the Fawn.
**Cannot free Woot at all** by any magic known to fairies or yookoohoos: the Green Monkey must exist in Oz for all future time and can only be transferred to someone else.
States plainly that Glinda's power in transformations is no greater than her own.
Refuses to force the form on any unwilling person, saying that would make them as cruel and wicked as Mrs. Yoop.
Adopts Polychrome's solution — giving the Green Monkey's form to its own creator — and performs it at a distance using a silver broth in a platter and her Wand.
Tells the Tin Woodman there is no harm in asking Nimmie Amee whether she still wishes to marry him, and offers a grand wedding at the Emerald City.
Rules at the end that Chopfyt need not be considered at all, and that they have no just cause to blame Ku-Klip.
Takes Captain Fyter into her service and sends him to keep order in the Gillikin Country, since two identical tin men could not live together in harmony.

known_facts_book1: A little Kansas girl living in Ozma's palace, who came to Oz in a house carried by a cyclone and never seems a day older.
Is the one who idly wishes to see the Tin Woodman in the Magic Picture and so discovers the journey, and who watches the transformations with indignation and horror.
Travels with Ozma and Toto in the Red Wagon to Jinjur's ranch and greets each transformed friend by name.
Refuses point-blank to let Toto be made a Green Monkey to free Woot — 'I don't want a green monkey'.
Is the one whose falling house crushed the Wicked Witch of the East, though in this book that is background: the Witch turned to dust and blew away.
Took the Witch's Silver Shoes to the Emerald City, which is why Nimmie Amee could not find them.
Does not go on the second half of the journey, because the Tin Woodman does not invite her and she will not intrude on his courtship.
Remarks at the end that it would have been wasteful for Ku-Klip not to have used the cast-off parts.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: Her dearest friend, whose Magic Picture she uses.

known_facts_book1: A girl farmer of the Munchkin Country who once raised an army of girls, called herself General Jinjur, captured the Emerald City and drove the Scarecrow out of it.
Was punished by Ozma for that, and afterward she and the Scarecrow became fast friends.
Now lives peacefully on a ranch raising fields of cream-puffs, chocolate-caramels and macaroons.
Is an artist who paints pictures so perfect one can scarcely tell them from nature; she once painted the Scarecrow a straw-stack he could stuff himself from.
Repaints the Scarecrow's face when it gets worn or mussy, and had done so about a month before the transformations.
Attacks the transformed party with a broomstick, taking them for wild animals, and knocks the Brown Bear over before he can explain.
Scrubs the sooty Green Monkey in a tub of cold water with a stiff brush and yellow soap, over his whines and struggles.
Argues that all persons are judged by the shapes in which they appear to others, and comforts Woot when Ozma cannot help him.
Gives Woot a basket of ripe cream-puffs and caramels when the party leaves.

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's shaggy little black dog and faithful companion, who rides in the Red Wagon because he cannot keep up with the Sawhorse.
Growls at the Tin Owl and is reproved by Dorothy several times for it.
Is proposed as the recipient of the Green Monkey's form and refuses flatly: 'I wouldn't become a Green Monkey for anything.'
Says being a dog is at least a matter of opinion when Woot claims a green monkey is better than a dog.
Appears only in the Emerald City chapters and takes no part in the journey.
